column1: What is the primary argument used by Saint Irenaeus of Lyon (Adv. Haer. III, 1–3) to refute Gnostic claims of secret oral traditions?
column2:
If the Apostles had known hidden mysteries taught secretly to the "perfect", they would have entrusted them first of all to the bishops to whom they committed the churches. Because episcopal succession is public and visible worldwide (traditio apostolorum in toto mundo manifestata), Gnostic secrecy is a false innovation.

🧠 Mnemonic: NO BACKROOM SECRETS: If the Apostles had secret treasures, they would give them to their appointed bishops, not underground sect gurus!

column1: Why does Saint Irenaeus single out the Church of Rome in Adversus Haereses III, 3.2, and what famous Latin formula does he use?
column2:
Because enumerating the succession of all churches would take too long, he points to the greatest, oldest, and universally known Church founded by Peter and Paul: "Ad hanc enim ecclesiam propter potentiorem principalitatem necesse est omnem convenire ecclesiam" (Every church must agree with this Church on account of its preeminent authority).

🧠 Mnemonic: POTENTIOREM PRINCIPALITATEM: Rome holds the louder trumpet and the prime apostolic benchmark.

column1: What are the 12 links in Saint Irenaeus's episcopal succession list of the Church of Rome from the Apostles to his day?
column2:
1. Linus (2 Tim 4:21)
2. Anacletus
3. Clement (author of 1 Clement)
4. Evaristus
5. Alexander
6. Sixtus
7. Telesphorus (martyr)
8. Hyginus
9. Pius
10. Anicetus
11. Soter
12. Eleutherus (12th bishop in Irenaeus's time).

🧠 Mnemonic: THE ROMAN TWELVE: Linus to Eleutherus: unbroken chain proving the deposit was never dropped.

column1: What is the theological meaning of Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger's formula: "Apostolic succession is the form of tradition; apostolic tradition is the content of succession"?
column2:
1. Form (Forma): Succession is the living, personal, historical structure (the bishops) through which the Gospel is handed down.
2. Content (Contentum): Tradition is the objective Deposit of Faith. The bishop is not an inventor, but a servant/custodian who withdraws behind what he received; without succession, tradition degenerates into ideology.

🧠 Mnemonic: FORM & CONTENT: Succession is the glass (form); Tradition is the pure wine inside (content). Neither exists in history without the other!

column1: What does Saint Clement of Rome witness in 1 Clement 44:2–3 (c. 96 AD) concerning the succession of ministers?
column2:
The Apostles foresaw that there would be strife over the episcopal office; therefore, they appointed ministers and gave orders that upon their death, other approved men should succeed them in their ministry with the consent of the whole Church.

🧠 Mnemonic: CLEMENT'S CLOCKWORK: 96 AD proves succession was not a 2nd-century emergency invention, but planned apostolic succession from the beginning.

column1: What 5 prerogatives belonged exclusively to the Twelve Apostles and ceased definitively with the death of the last Apostle (non-transmissible)?
column2:
1. Direct vocation by Christ (historical election).
2. Eyewitnesses of the Risen Lord (Acts 1:21–22).
3. Foundational role of the Church (Eph 2:20).
4. Constitutive public revelation (closed with the death of the last Apostle).
5. Universal personal jurisdiction & biblical inspiration.

🧠 Mnemonic: FOUNDATION STONES DON'T FLOAT: The foundation is laid once at the ground floor; bishops build the upper storeys.

column1: What elements of the apostolic ministry are transmissible and permanently endure in the order of bishops (Lumen Gentium 20)?
column2:
The threefold pastoral office (tria munera): preaching the Gospel (munus docendi), sanctifying through the sacraments and Eucharist (munus sanctificandi), and shepherding the flock in governance (munus regendi), empowered by the sacra potestas.

🧠 Mnemonic: TRIA MUNERA ENDURES: Teaching, Sanctifying, Governing continues until the end of the age.

column1: According to the Council of Trent (Session XXIII) and Lumen Gentium 20, who alone are the true successors of the Apostles?
column2:
The Bishops alone (episcopos, qui in apostolorum locum successerunt). Presbyters and deacons are necessary collaborators in a subordinate degree, but only bishops possess the apostolic succession in its fullness.

🧠 Mnemonic: BISHOPS ONLY IN APEX: Solus episcopus is the direct successor; priests are his right hand.

column1: How does Tertullian formulate the "apostolic criterion" against early heretics in De Praescriptione Haereticorum (ch. 32)?
column2:
He challenges heretics to roll out the list of their bishops (evolvant ordinem episcoporum suorum), proving an unbroken chain back to an apostle as their predecessor and guarantor. If they cannot, they have no apostolic seed.

🧠 Mnemonic: ROLL OUT THE SCROLL: Show me your family tree, or you're a theological squatter!

column1: Why is the concept of "participation" in Christ's priesthood essential to prevent the multiplication of priesthoods (Goyret, Ch. 3)?
column2:
Because if ministerial priests did not participate in the one unique priesthood of Christ, there would be many independent priesthoods. The bishop/priest does not receive an autonomous power to use at will; rather, Christ Himself is present and acts as principal agent through the minister as His instrument.

🧠 Mnemonic: NO CLONED PRIESTS: Participation means Christ is the Singer; the priest is merely His microphone.

column1: Why does 1 Peter 2:25 call Christ the "pastorem et episcopum animarum vestrarum" in relation to the hierarchy?
column2:
It shows that the episcopal ministry of bishops is the sacramental visibility of Christ's own episcopate. The veneration given to bishops rests on the fact that Christ the Shepherd-Bishop is made visibly present in their person and action.

🧠 Mnemonic: EPISCOPUS VISIBILIS: The earthly bishop makes the unseen Shepherd-Bishop tangible to the flock.

column1: Why can the cultic dimension (consecration) and the evangelising dimension (mission) never be existentially separated in the priest (Goyret, Ch. 3)?
column2:
Because man is chosen from among men (assumptus / consecration) precisely on behalf of men in relation to God (pro hominibus / mission, Heb 5:1). A priest who only performs cult without mission falls into ritualism; one who only does social work without cult abandons his divine consecration.

🧠 Mnemonic: CONSECRATION FOR MISSION: Inseparable two sides of the same coin: worship God to serve men; serve men to lead them to worship.
